Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with
complaints of neck pain and low back pain, along with stiffness and reduced range of
motion in both regions. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the force
and direction of the impact, and the presenting symptoms align well with that
mechanism. Cervical and lumbar examination findings were objective, including
documented muscle guarding and limited motion, and imaging studies clearly confirm the
soft tissue injury to both areas. No prior injury to the cervical or lumbar spine is
known from the hisotry obtained. Care was delivered over eleven visits, consisting of
manual therapy, guided home exercise, and graduated activity instruction. Treatment
continued somewhat longer than is typical for a strain of this type, reflecting a
slower functional recovery. Billing records reflect single entries for each service
rendered with no repeated or duplicate charges. The patient has been advised to
continue home exercises and to return if symptoms worsen.
